To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) hard-positive and hard negative examples, selected by 3D models reconstructed from the query images, improve particular object retrieval, (ii) whitening of CNN image descriptors discriminatively learned from 3D models improves retrieval performance, and (iii) a novel trainable GeM pooling improves retrieval performance.

1) fine-tuning of CNNs for image search can be performed in an automated manner, using only the 3D geometry of the images, 2) hard-positive and hard-negatives selected from the training data improve retrieval performance, and 3) a novel trainable GeM pooling layer outperforms max and average pooling.
fine-tuning CNN image retrieval with no human annotation is feasible and can lead to state-of-the-art results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to fine-tune a pre-trained network for image retrieval on unordered data without human annotation.
the question: how to train a Convolutional Neural Network for image retrieval without any human annotation?
the problem of fine-tuning CNNs for image search in a fully automated way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method outperforms the state of the art by a large margin on all three datasets.
the proposed method is a significant step towards automatic fine-tuning of deep networks for image retrieval, which can be applied to any dataset without human annotation.
our approach is the first to demonstrate that CNNs can be trained in a fully automated fashion, using no human-annotated data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

fine-tuning a CNN on a large collection with no human annotation can outperform the same network trained from scratch on a small collection of images with human annotations, and the performance is even comparable to a network trained from scratch with the same amount of human-annotated training data as the large collection.
fine-tuning a CNN for image retrieval can be performed in a fully automated way without human annotation.
fine-tuning CNNs with no human annotation is possible and can achieve state-of-the-art results in image retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retrieval performance of CNNs can be significantly improved without using any human annotation.

the quality of training data can be improved significantly by exploiting 3D models reconstructed automatically from the image collection, and this improvement translates to a substantial performance increase in image retrieval.
fine-tuning CNN image descriptors on a large-scale collection of unordered images, using no human annotation whatsoever, can achieve performance on par with the state-of-the art.
